presentations.presentation_title: Multi-instrument and Multi-station Observations and Predictions of Ionospheric Irregularities (mopii) in the East-asia Sector
presentations.abstract: In this study, a multi-station and multi-instrument system, organized and proposed for ionospheric scintillation and equatorial spread-F specification and their associated motions in the East-Asia sector, is outlined. We first demonstrate the observations of ionospheric irregularities or equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) using the FormoSat-7 / Constellation Observing System for Meteorology, Ionosphere and Climate-2 (FS7/COSMIC2) GPS/GLONASS radio occultation observations. The obtained seasonal–longitudinal distributions of EPBs presented two diffused traces of high occurrence rates, which happened near the days and longitudes when and where the angle between the two lines of magnetic declination and solar terminator at the magnetic equator was equal to zero. We verify the latitudinal extent of the tracked plasma bubble in the Taiwan-Philippines sector using the recorded ionograms from the Vertical Incidence Pulsed Ionospheric Radar (VIPIR) located at Hualien, Taiwan. We further discuss the spatial and temporal variabilities of two-dimensional EPB maps and/or vertical scintillation index VS 4 maps based on an all-sky nightglow imaging network and the simultaneous GPS L1-band signal measurements from 133 ground-based receivers located in Taiwan and nearby islands. We also operate two high-sampling software-defined GPS receivers and characterize the targeted plasma irregularities by carrying out spectrum analyses of the received signal. As a result, we present the climatological and seasonal–longitudinal variability of EPB occurrences, compare the results with the physical Rayleigh-Taylor instability model, and propose EPBs to be controlled by pre-reversal enhancement (PRE) fields.

presentations.presentation_title: Modeling Equatorial Plasma Bubbles During the 2024 Mother’s Day Storm with SAMI3/WACCM-X
presentations.abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) during the 2024 Mother’s Day storm using the one-way coupled SAMI3 and WACCM-X models. Notably, the SAMI3/WACCM-X self-consistently generates large-scale super EPBs without incorporating the physics of storm-indued penetration electric fields, which are conventionally considered the primary drivers of super EPBs during geomagnetic storms. The EPBs extend to midlatitudes, exhibit distorted structures, and persist into the post-sunrise hours, displaying the post-sunrise EPB characteristics. The formation of these EPBs is associated with the storm-indued neutral wind variations, specifically those associated with the Disturbance Dynamo Electric Field (DDEF). A comparative simulation using NRLMSIS neutral densities and temperatures, along with WACCMX neutral winds, was conducted. The super EPBs again developed, demonstrating the critical role of neutral wind perturbations. Although EPBs form in both simulations, differences in ionospheric background conditions significantly influence their morphology and longitudinal distribution.

presentations.presentation_title: Persisting Daytime Equatorial Plasma Bubbles Over Asia-pacific Region Following the Geomagnetic Storms
presentations.abstract: We investigated the strong geomagnetic storm occurred on 01-December-2023 that triggered unusual equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) over 100-140°E longitudes and persisted for several hours after sunrise. Utilizing FORMOSAT-7/COSMIC-2 and ground-based global navigation satellite system observations of slant TECs, the Global Ionospheric Specification (GIS) was built for providing electron density structure in three-dimensions with temporal resolution of 30 mins. GIS is used to investigate this long-lasting unseasonal EPB episode in the solstice period over Asia-Pacific. The results show that in presence of elevated F-layer bottom-side aided by prompt penetration electric field (PPEF) and large-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances (LSTIDs) traveling from high- to low-latitudes could possibly seed the instability soon right after sunset to generate a rapid growth of EPBs for phase one. In phase two, reinforced EPBs generation in the post-midnight period triggered by another group of larger LSTIDs that uncharacteristically prolonged into daytime hours and lasted until noon. GIS observations further provide evidence that the extremely low background ionization on the following day due to composition changes during negative storm phase enabled these EPBs to survive even after sunrise before the depleted flux tubes were refilled by fresh ionization. The coordinated ground- and space-based observations demonstrate the causal links for the rare unseasonal EPBs occurring in the post-sunset and post-midnight periods over the same longitude sector and the latter persisting several hours after sunrise. This study will also present similar long-lasting EPB events driven by other geomagnetic storms.

presentations.presentation_title: Response of global low-latitude ionospheric irregularities during the magnetic storms in January 2025
presentations.institution: National Space Science Center, Chinese Academy of Sciences
presentations.abstract: Between the end of 2024 and the beginning of 2025, two consecutive magnetic storms occurred. The first one, a strong magnetic storm, took place from December 31st to January 3rd, with the Dst index reaching a minimum of -212 nT at 15-16 UT on the 1st. The second one, a moderate magnetic storm, occurred from January 4th to 6th, with the Dst index reaching a minimum of -92 nT at 10 UT on the 4th. These two magnetic storms had significantly different impacts on the ionospheric irregularity activities in different low-latitude regions on the globe. Using ground-based GPS observations, COSMIC2, and SWARM satellite observations, the responses of global low-latitude ionospheric irregularity activities during these two magnetic storms were analyzed. The main results showed that: (1) During the main phase and recovery phase of the strong magnetic storm (from the 31st to the 2nd), nighttime ionospheric irregularity activities in the South America-Atlantic region (-70º ~10º) were significantly suppressed, even disappearing completely. (2) In the East Asia-West Pacific region (90º-160º), there was a significant enhancement of ionospheric irregularity activities during the strong magnetic storm (from the 1st to the 2nd). These rregularities were most intense in the West Pacific region, mainly occurring during the main phase and recovery phase of the magnetic storm, and could persist from night to day. (3) In the East Pacific region, nighttime ionospheric irregularity activities occurred during both magnetic storms, which were significantly intensified during the recovery phase of the magnetic storm on the 4th, persisting from night to day. During magnetic storms, the combined effects of prompt penetration electric field and disturbed dynamo electric field play an important role in suppressing or enhancing ionospheric irregularity activities in different low-latitude regions.
